fields.statement: Verifier claude-code-e530f80a at 84bda078: go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(health|health-projects|health-runs-cap|describe-golden|watchdog-health|daemon-version-in-health|daemon-status.*)$' -count=1 passes, with GOTMPDIR moved outside ~/code/rhiza (the run's GOTMPDIR sits inside the main repo, so every script's rhiza init otherwise finds its .rhiza). The new health-runs-cap.txtar uses two projects' fake daemon state. With max_runs 4, two live runs in alpha, one in beta and starting 1, health prints 'ok daemon running' and 'runs: 3/4 live, 1 starting', and health --json carries live 3, starting 1, max 4. With max_runs 2 it prints 'bad daemon running', 'runs: 3/2 live, 1 starting' and 'live run: alpha, RUNA1' / 'alpha, RUNA2' / 'beta, RUNB1', and exits 1. Diff read: daemon.State gains Starting, set at saveState from pending starts, request starts and resumes within daemonStartGrace; healthRunsAgainstCap sums live (an interrupted run takes no slot) and starting across projects and is bad when live+starting > maxRuns, adding one detail line per live run (project, run, change set title, which falls back to the ID). go vet is clean. go test ./internal/api -run 'Health|Daemon|Start': every test PASS. The package was then marked FAIL only by the enclosing-root guard on ~/code/.rhiza-root/usage.live.json, which the live root daemon rewrites (mtime changed with no test running); the leaf touches no usage code.
